legacy_rationale: The benchmark evaluates professional legal competency through multiple-choice questions and essays that require applying legal principles to specific fact patterns.
The benchmark evaluates capability on high-level biology competition problems, which requires deep specialized knowledge and the ability to reason through complex biological scenarios.
HumanEval evaluates the functional correctness of Python code synthesis based on function signatures and docstrings.
The benchmark consists of multi-step grade school math word problems that require chain-of-thought reasoning to reach a solution.
The GRE is a standardized graduate entrance exam evaluating verbal reasoning, quantitative reasoning, and analytical writing, serving as a general benchmark for academic logic and aptitude.

This benchmark tests massive multi-discipline understanding by requiring models to process visual inputs (charts, diagrams, images) and reason across diverse college-level subjects ranging from arts to engineering.
The benchmark evaluates diverse multitask language understanding and complex multi-step reasoning across a wide breadth of subjects including STEM, humanities, and social sciences.

DROP requires models to perform discrete reasoning operations (such as addition, counting, or sorting) over paragraphs of general text to generate answers.
The benchmark is a suite of diverse, challenging tasks requiring multi-step chain-of-thought reasoning across logic, arithmetic, and general knowledge domains.
CoVoST 2 is a large-scale multilingual speech-to-text translation benchmark involving audio processing, classifying it as Multimodal Perception.
HellaSwag evaluates commonsense reasoning by challenging models to complete contexts with plausible endings that require physical and situational understanding.
This benchmark evaluates the code generation capabilities of models by assessing their ability to translate natural language instructions into functional code.
FLEURS is a speech dataset covering 102 languages used for evaluating automatic speech recognition and speech translation.
The benchmark evaluates visual question answering capabilities on infographics, requiring the interpretation of complex layouts, text, and data visualizations.

The benchmark requires models to perceive and reason about text embedded within images to answer natural language questions.
VATEX is a large-scale dataset for video captioning and retrieval, requiring models to interpret visual and audio inputs to generate multilingual text descriptions.
VQAv2 evaluates a model's ability to answer natural language questions based on visual inputs, requiring multimodal understanding of general scenes.

GPQA contains graduate-level questions in biology, physics, and chemistry designed to defeat simple retrieval, thereby requiring deep reasoning to solve.
The benchmark evaluates general fluid intelligence through abstract visual-grid puzzles that require logical deduction, spatial reasoning, and pattern abstraction.
MGSM is a multilingual extension of the GSM8K benchmark, requiring multi-step chain-of-thought reasoning to solve grade-school mathematics word problems across different languages.
AI2D involves diagram understanding, which requires multimodal perception and general commonsense reasoning.
The benchmark requires answering questions based on visual charts involving data interpretation and logical/arithmetic reasoning.
EgoSchema evaluates very long-term video understanding and temporal reasoning using egocentric footage and multiple-choice questions.
ActivityNet involves understanding and perceiving activities in videos, which falls under multimodal perception and general commonsense understanding of human actions.
M3Exam is a benchmark consisting of actual human exam questions from varying levels and languages that requires interpreting both text and visual inputs across diverse subjects.
AIME consists of challenging mathematics competition problems that require deep, multi-step logical reasoning and calculation.
The benchmark consists of competitive programming problems that require complex algorithmic reasoning and code generation to solve.

The benchmark consists of elite-level mathematical olympiad problems requiring complex, multi-step logical reasoning and proof generation.

Evaluates multimodal agents executing multi-step open-ended tasks within a real computer operating system environment, interacting with various software applications and interfaces.
The benchmark evaluates large language models on code generation, self-repair, and test output prediction using recent competitive programming problems to ensure contamination-free assessment.
Evaluates multi-turn or multilingual reasoning capabilities, likely involving reading comprehension or context retrieval.
Vibe-Eval is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal chat models on challenging visual prompts requiring image understanding and nuance.
The benchmark evaluates text-to-SQL generation capabilities by requiring models to reason over database schemas and contents to write complex SQL queries.
The benchmark evaluates the model's ability to produce factually accurate, grounded responses and avoid hallucinations across a broad range of general topics.
HiddenMath is an internal held-out dataset of competitive math problems described in the Gemini technical report, requiring multi-step generative reasoning.
This benchmark evaluates the performance of multimodal agents in navigating and interacting with real-world websites to complete end-to-end user tasks.
FrontierMath consists of expert-level original research mathematics problems requiring deep, multi-step generative reasoning to solve.
SimpleQA measures the factuality and calibration of language models on a diverse set of short-answer general knowledge questions.
The benchmark evaluates the model's ability to reason through and generate correct code solutions for programming problems sourced from recent contests and libraries.

MATH 500 is a subset of the larger MATH dataset consisting of competition-level mathematics problems that require complex multi-step reasoning to solve.
The benchmark evaluates autonomous software engineering agents by tasking them to resolve real-world GitHub issues through codebase exploration and patch generation.
A multidisciplinary, multimodal benchmark designed to test expert-level abstract reasoning and problem-solving capabilities across diverse academic fields.
The benchmark evaluates the model's ability to solve difficult coding problems by generating and editing code across multiple programming languages.
The benchmark evaluates logical and algorithmic reasoning by asking models to determine connectivity or paths within graph structures described in text.
The benchmark evaluates multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities using charts and figures extracted from scientific arXiv papers.
This benchmark evaluates instruction following by testing a model's ability to adhere to multiple concurrent constraints and formatting requirements within a single prompt.
The benchmark evaluates AI agents on real-world software engineering tasks derived from freelance platforms, requiring multi-step planning, tool use, and codebase interaction.
COLLIE evaluates the ability of LLMs to generate text that adheres to specific linguistic and structural constraints.

The benchmark evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models on their ability to process, perceive, and answer questions about video content across various durations and general domains.
BrowseComp evaluates web browsing agents on their ability to navigate websites, interact with page elements, and retrieve information to complete tasks.
The benchmark evaluates language model agents on their ability to execute commands and solve tasks within a Linux terminal environment.

This benchmark evaluates multimodal models on college-level reasoning tasks across diverse disciplines (including Science, Art, and Humanities) using video inputs.
HMMT consists of high-school level mathematics competition problems used to evaluate multi-step mathematical reasoning capabilities.
The benchmark evaluates entity-relation question answering capabilities, requiring the model to retrieve and connect factual information regarding entities and their relationships.

The benchmark evaluates autonomous agents on their ability to perform multi-step financial analysis and tasks using tools.
The benchmark evaluates the model's ability to autonomously solve multi-step technical tasks by interacting with a command-line terminal environment.
The benchmark evaluates GUI grounding capabilities by requiring models to visually locate specific interface elements within screenshots based on textual instructions.
The benchmark evaluates long-horizon agentic operation of a simulated vending-machine business, including tool use, purchasing, pricing, supplier negotiation, and delayed operational consequences.
This composite factuality suite combines parametric knowledge, search, multimodal, and grounding evaluations; the v2 category is a headline projection rather than a single exclusive construct.
A crowdsourced open platform evaluating LLMs via pairwise human voting on a wide range of diverse, general-purpose user queries.
Global PIQA evaluates physical commonsense reasoning capabilities across multiple languages using a multiple-choice question answering format.
The benchmark evaluates language models on their ability to solve complex mathematical problems requiring multi-step reasoning.

This benchmark evaluates Large Multimodal Models on comprehensive document understanding tasks, including text recognition, layout analysis, and chart/table interpretation across various document types.
Scale MCP-Atlas evaluates agentic tool use through multi-step tasks across MCP servers for search, productivity, analytics, finance, coding, and external data connections.
The benchmark evaluates general fluid intelligence and skill acquisition through few-shot abstract reasoning puzzles on grid-based inputs.
The benchmark evaluates autonomous software engineering capabilities by requiring agents to solve real-world GitHub issues across multiple programming languages within repository contexts.
The benchmark evaluates autonomous web agents on their ability to navigate websites and interact with web elements to complete diverse browsing tasks.
This benchmark evaluates AI agents by testing their ability to interact with and manage the state of a simulated vending machine through multi-step reasoning and actions.
This benchmark evaluates multi-round conversational reasoning capabilities, requiring models to maintain logical consistency and context tracking across extended dialogue turns.
The benchmark evaluates autonomous software engineering agents on their ability to navigate large codebases, write code, and pass tests to resolve real-world issues.

GDPval evaluates realistic knowledge-work deliverables across many occupations and economically significant sectors; the specialized-domain label is a broad v2 projection rather than an economics-only interpretation.
Toolathlon evaluates the ability of language models to plan and execute multi-step tasks using external tools and APIs across diverse scenarios.
The benchmark converts BrowseComp-style agentic questions into long-context retrieval tasks that require finding relevant information in noisy in-context data rather than live web navigation.
This benchmark evaluates large language models on complex legal research and drafting tasks designed to simulate the work of associates at major law firms.
GDPval-AA is Artificial Analysis' agentic real-world knowledge-work evaluation over GDPval-style tasks with file outputs and pairwise scoring; the specialized-domain label is a broad v2 projection.
OSWorld-Verified is the verified OSWorld benchmark update for computer-use agents, with fixed examples, updated results, and real desktop task execution across everyday operating-system workflows.
CyberGym functions as an interactive environment for evaluating autonomous agents on cybersecurity tasks, requiring multi-step decision making and system interaction.
The benchmark evaluates execution of bioinformatics workflows with access to bash, code execution, package managers, and specialized computational-biology reasoning.

This benchmark evaluates the ability to perform root cause analysis on cloud computing incidents, requiring complex reasoning over system logs and topology data within the domain of software engineering.

SWE-Lancer IC Diamond is the independent-contributor Diamond track/split of SWE-Lancer, evaluating real-world software engineering tasks with end-to-end tests; kept separate because the release page reports this track explicitly.
APEX-Agents evaluates long-horizon professional workflows for AI agents, using realistic tasks from domains such as finance, consulting, and law that require tool use and multi-step deliverables.
SciCode evaluates code generation for realistic scientific research tasks, requiring models to combine domain knowledge, reasoning, and programming across natural-science problems.
The benchmark evaluates competitive programming and algorithmic reasoning on continuously updated problems from Codeforces, ICPC, and IOI, reducing contamination risk while testing code synthesis.

FinanceAgent v1.1 is Vals AI's updated Finance Agent benchmark for core financial analyst tasks, preserving the explicit version label from the GPT-5.4 release page.

OpenAI describes this as an internal spreadsheet-modeling benchmark for junior investment banking analyst work; kept as a separate private/internal eval because the release page reports it as an Eval row.
CoT-Control is an OpenAI evaluation suite for measuring whether reasoning models can follow chain-of-thought control instructions that could reduce monitorability.
Frontier Science Research is the research track of OpenAI's FrontierScience benchmark, evaluating expert-level open-ended scientific reasoning tasks graded with rubrics.

OfficeQA evaluates agents on grounded multi-document reasoning over business and financial document corpora, requiring parsing, retrieval, computation, and analytical reasoning across heterogeneous office documents.

OmniDocBench evaluates document understanding across text recognition, layout, table, formula, and chart parsing; kept separate from OmniDocBench 1.5 because the GPT-5.4 release page reports the unversioned name.
Online-Mind2Web evaluates web agents on diverse multi-step tasks across live websites, measuring browser-use task completion in realistic online settings.
WebArena-Verified is a verified release of WebArena for browser agents, with audited tasks and deterministic evaluation for web interaction.
Anthropic describes an automated behavioral audit used to score misaligned behavior, making it a safety/alignment evaluation that should be kept distinct until reviewed.
OfficeQA Pro evaluates AI agents on grounded multi-document reasoning over a large heterogeneous corpus, requiring document parsing, retrieval, computation, and analytical reasoning.
An early-access tester reports a 93-task coding benchmark for long-running coding workflows and task resolution, so it is preserved as a private partner evaluation.

Notion reports implicit-need tests for complex multi-step workflows, suggesting an agentic task-completion evaluation with implicit requirements and tool-failure recovery.

Qodo reports a real-world code review benchmark for identifying issues and reviewing code, requiring coding-domain reasoning and precision.

CritPt evaluates research-level physics reasoning with frontier physics problems that require symbolic, numerical, or programmatic answers.
Expert-SWE is OpenAI's internal frontier software-engineering evaluation for long-horizon coding tasks with a median estimated human completion time of 20 hours.
GeneBench evaluates AI agents on multi-stage scientific data analysis in genetics and quantitative biology, including ambiguous data, quality-control issues, and statistical-method interpretation.
IFBench evaluates single-turn instruction following across precise counting, formatting, and sentence-manipulation constraints.
